title: Quantized transport of two-dimensional multifrequency solitons
authors: Fangwei Ye, Yaroslav V. Kartashov, Vladimir V. Konotop
abstract: We consider Thouless pumping of two-dimensional quadratic solitons composed from coherently interacting fundamental frequency (FF) and second harmonic (SH) components propagating in a periodic $χ^{(2)}$ material. The pumping is induced by two mutually sliding two-dimensional lattices defined by shallow transverse and longitudinal periodic refractive index modulation. Focusing on solitons in the semi-infinite gap, we find three distinct pumping scenarios: the absence of transport for small-amplitude solitons, non-quantized transport in a transient regime at intermediate amplitudes, and stable quantized transport for solitons with relatively large amplitudes. Different directions of the sliding velocity were investigated resulting in different trajectories of soliton center. The transition to the regime of quantized transport is found to depend strongly on phase mismatch between FF and SH waves that also influences stability properties of two-dimensional $χ^{(2)}$ lattice solitons. We also show that pumping with longitudinal periods in the x and y directions, whose ratio approximates an irrational number, induces quantized transport whose direction rapidly converges, with increase of the accuracy of the approximation, to a limiting pumping direction determined by this irrational number and corresponding to truly incommensurate longitudinal periods.
summary: This paper theoretically studies the quantized transport of two-dimensional solitons composed of two interacting optical frequencies (FF and SH) within a periodic nonlinear crystal. It establishes that the transport mechanism, known as Thouless pumping, is robust and can be controlled by the phase mismatch and the commensurability of the underlying lattice modulation. The findings extend the concept of topological pumping to complex 2D, multifrequency nonlinear systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the quantized transport (Thouless pumping) of two-dimensional multifrequency solitons.
main_result: Stable, quantized topological transport is demonstrated for 2D solitons in $\chi^{(2)}$ nonlinear materials, persisting even when the lattice modulation periods are incommensurate.
method: The analysis uses the adiabatic approximation applied to coupled nonlinear wave equations, supplemented by linear spectral analysis and topological invariants like Chern numbers.
model_or_system: The system involves two-dimensional quadratic solitons composed of coherently interacting fundamental frequency (FF) and second harmonic (SH) components propagating in a periodic $\chi^{(2)}$ material.
key_observables: Quantized center-of-mass displacement, power imbalance between FF and SH components, and the ratio of lattice periods converging to irrational numbers (e.g., the golden ratio).
important_parameters: Phase mismatch ($ eta$), soliton amplitude, and the ratio of longitudinal lattice periods ($Z_x/Z_y$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the adiabatic character of the pumping process and utilizes approximations based on the quasi-stationary solutions of the coupled nonlinear equations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the linear spectrum and the dependence of soliton profiles on phase mismatch ($ eta$), and show the center-of-mass trajectories in the $(x, y)$ plane, demonstrating convergence towards irrational ratios.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the governing coupled nonlinear equations to analyzing the linear spectrum and topological invariants, then detailing the three pumping regimes based on soliton amplitude, and finally extending the analysis to incommensurate lattice modulation.
why_interesting: This work bridges nonlinear optics, topological physics, and condensed matter concepts (like Bloch bands and pumping), providing a robust theoretical framework for understanding topological phenomena in nonlinear wave systems.
